item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-a0dfdaa2c03e0d9a","start_unit":9,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"On 8 January 2023, Bolsonaro supporters invaded Brazil's Congress, Supreme Court, and presidential palace in an attempted coup; the article reports the attack was frustrated.","question_ids":["3B.9","4B.1","4B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; Lula inherited and responded to the crisis.","ruler_attribution":"The event was carried out by Bolsonaro supporters, not attributed to Lula.","limitations":["The article is an academic discussion and relies partly on cited press reports."]},{"source_id":"SRC-27091718bb9de921","start_unit":10,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The article identifies Brazil's 2015–2021 secular stagnation as involving cumulative GDP growth of -3.6%, unemployment above 10%, and causes including contractionary policy, political-institutional crisis, COVID-19, and deindustrialization.","question_ids":["5B.7","5B.9","5B.10"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Background inherited by Lula in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes the period's conditions primarily to post-2015 governments and external shocks, not Lula's 2023 administration.","limitations":["The evidence predates 2023 and is a macroeconomic interpretation rather than an evaluation of Lula's 2023 execution."]},{"source_id":"SRC-27091718bb9de921","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Brazil's 2020 government implemented countercyclical fiscal, monetary, and social measures totaling about 8% of GDP; GDP fell 4.1%, better than the IMF's then-expected 9.1% decline, while unemployment rose to 13.5%.","question_ids":["5B.9","6B.6"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Historical comparator relevant to Lula's inherited macroeconomic and social baseline.","ruler_attribution":"The measures are attributed to Brazilian economic authorities during the Bolsonaro period, not Lula.","limitations":["Not evidence about Lula's 2023 decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-45fd9b7a9cb067d1","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"After the 8 January 2023 attack, Lula declared an emergency and dismissed several senior security officials appointed under Bolsonaro.","question_ids":["3B.9","4B.4","4B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes the emergency declaration and dismissals to Lula.","limitations":["The article is a contemporaneous analytical commentary and gives no detailed account of subsequent legal proceedings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-45fd9b7a9cb067d1","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"The 2023 transition authorized approximately $28 billion in additional spending outside Brazil's constitutional spending cap for social welfare and public works.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly relevant to Lula's 2023 budget choices.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes the suspension of the spending cap and additional spending authorization to Lula's incoming government and Congress.","limitations":["The source warns of fiscal risks and does not establish final expenditure quality or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-45fd9b7a9cb067d1","start_unit":12,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"Lula's government proposed replacing the spending cap with a fiscal framework combining a 70% ceiling on real spending growth relative to real revenue growth, a 2.5% maximum real spending increase, and primary-balance targets.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the 2023 policy program.","ruler_attribution":"The framework is attributed to Lula's government and its legislative initiative.","limitations":["At the article's publication, the framework was still under legislative consideration; implementation and outcomes were unresolved."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7825b3f0b1ea6e79","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"IPEA published a 2023 working paper analyzing Brazil's emergency cash transfer during COVID-19 in comparison with the United States stimulus check.","question_ids":["6B.5","6B.6"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The publication is from 2023, but its subject is the earlier pandemic period.","ruler_attribution":"No Lula-specific policy or outcome is stated in the supplied units.","limitations":["The supplied page contains metadata only, not the paper's findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-17fa423dc68af603","start_unit":1,"end_unit":1,"fact_summary":"Brazil's Federal Court of Accounts reviewed Lula's 2023 presidential accounts, including macroeconomic policy, fiscal policy, debt, budget execution, program results, legal compliance, financial statements, and follow-up of prior recommendations.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 Lula administration.","ruler_attribution":"The TCU identifies Lula as the head of the Executive responsible for the 2023 accounts.","limitations":["The supplied unit describes the audit scope but does not provide the findings, opinion, or recommendations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bbc8ddb8911c7e29","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"In 2023 Lula's government restored Bolsa Família, benefiting more than 21 million families with an average payment of R$672 and total transfers exceeding R$14 billion; it added R$150 per child under six and R$50 per pregnant woman.","question_ids":["5B.8","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.7","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes the restoration and supplements to Lula's third government.","limitations":["Coverage and payment figures are described as the government's latest balance available to the authors."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bbc8ddb8911c7e29","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"Lula's 2023 government relaunched Minha Casa, Minha Vida with a low-income faixa 1 and subsidies up to 95%, opened 15,000 new Mais Médicos positions, and raised the minimum wage in real terms by 3%, increasing 65% of INSS benefits tied to the wage floor.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measures are attributed to Lula's third government.","limitations":["The source describes enacted or announced measures but does not provide service-quality or longer-term outcome data."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bbc8ddb8911c7e29","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"The 2022 transition amendment opened R$145 billion in 2023 budget space, approximately matching the projected primary deficit of R$136 billion, and abolished the prior spending cap while requiring a replacement fiscal rule.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly relevant to Lula's 2023 fiscal framework.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes the political agreement and resulting fiscal space to Lula's transition and incoming government.","limitations":["The source presents both social-policy capacity and fiscal-risk implications; it does not itself adjudicate sustainability."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bbc8ddb8911c7e29","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The editorial estimates that federal social spending grew 70% in real terms during Lula's first two administrations, while the proposed 2023 fiscal framework would cap annual real federal spending growth at 2.5%; it warns that this could constrain simultaneous expansion of social programs.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.10","6B.9","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The historical comparison and proposed constraint are relevant to 2023, but the outcome is prospective.","ruler_attribution":"The earlier spending growth is attributed to Lula's first two governments; the proposed constraint to his third government.","limitations":["The article is an editorial assessment and does not establish end-of-2023 social outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-81a69f0ec45a05a8","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Lula's 2023 election was described as ending Bolsonaro's government and creating a democratic opening, but the editorial argues that sustaining it requires public education to promote democratic culture and political participation.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.3","4B.10","6B.1"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the transition into Lula's 2023 mandate.","ruler_attribution":"The democratic opening is attributed to Lula's electoral victory; the need for further institutional and educational work is the authors' assessment.","limitations":["This is a normative editorial assessment rather than a quantified evaluation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-81a69f0ec45a05a8","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"The editorial reports that Lula's government strengthened SUS and resumed vaccination priority, restored the Ministry of Culture, and appointed figures with public commitments in strategic cultural, human-rights, Indigenous, racial-equality, science, and technology institutions; it also criticizes the education ministry for excluding collective education-sector interlocutors from central decisions.","question_ids":["4B.5","4B.7","5B.6","6B.2","6B.8","8B.4","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns early 2023 government practice.","ruler_attribution":"The measures and appointments are attributed to Lula's government; the education criticism is attributed to the editorial authors.","limitations":["The source provides no outcome measures for vaccination, institutional performance, or education policy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f846c3056416b3cb","start_unit":13,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"A longitudinal study finds that Lula's governments adopted and expanded targeted transfers through Bolsa Família, while maintaining core universalist institutions; it reports redistributive gains but constraints on federal spending growth in health, education, and sanitation and weak performance in education and sanitation.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.9","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Historical evidence from Lula's first two terms, relevant as a prior record and baseline for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The study attributes the policy choices and tradeoffs to Lula's 2003–2008 government.","limitations":["The study predates the 2023 term and cannot establish its outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4f9a71c222ff46d0","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"A study of Lula's 2003–2010 foreign-policy decision-making finds that the Foreign Ministry's structure remained stable while expanding, presidential diplomacy was used to expedite proceedings, regular bureaucratic processes were bypassed on sensitive issues, and the relative influence of career diplomats declined.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.5","7B.5","8B.4","8B.5"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Historical evidence from Lula's first two terms, not direct evidence for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings are attributed to Lula's 2003–2010 administration.","limitations":["The supplied source concerns an earlier period and foreign-policy bureaucracy, so transfer to 2023 is limited."]},{"source_id":"SRC-21f39f0f9c594bd1","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"A doctoral thesis finds that regional integration was a priority of Lula's 2003–2010 foreign policy and interprets pragmatic South American diplomacy as seeking Brazilian regional leadership and greater prominence internationally.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.10","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Historical evidence from Lula's first two terms, not direct evidence for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The thesis attributes the regional-integration priority and leadership strategy to Lula's governments.","limitations":["The supplied page contains the thesis abstract rather than detailed episode-level evidence."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-b18319f8f757d4f0","SRC-6ebb8a72a54e0ab0"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied documents concern Lula's earlier terms or Bolsonaro's administration; they are included only where they materially establish Lula's inherited baseline, prior record, or a direct comparison.","The supplied metadata page for SRC-7825b3f0b1ea6e79 does not contain substantive findings.","No supplied document provides material evidence for nuclear-risk questions 1B.1-1B.10, and no facts were mapped to them.","No scores or chapter judgments are provided."]}
